II. Chairperson’s Report Chairperson Eric McClure thanked the Van Alen Institute for hosting our meetings and noted that their ability to host hybrid meetings is a great asset to the board. He welcomed newly appointed board members to their first meeting as members and noted that Community Board service is an important way to get involved in the community. He announced that the Carroll Street Bridge will reopen on June 15th, with use limited to pedestrians, bikes, and emergency vehicles, in keeping with the motion previously passed by the Board. He noted that the bridge is one of only four retractile drawbridges in the United States and that limiting vehicle use will help sustain the bridge’s condition in the future.

March 11, 2026Full BoardTransportation / streets / parking

Tony explained that Safe Streets and Make McGuinness Safe presented at the last committee meeting.

Passedminutes ↗
Full text

Tony explained that Safe Streets and Make McGuinness Safe presented at the last committee meeting. He explained that the district-wide speed limit would apply only to streets with no more than two lanes in one direction, and that similar motions have been passed by Brooklyn Community Board 1 and Queens Community Board 2. The committee passed the resolution unanimously with one abstention for cause. Marc Torrence noted that while the reduction from 25 MPH to 20 MPH seems small, it significantly improves survivability in crashes. Tony noted that enforcement typically begins 10 MPH over the limit, meaning tickets would start at 30 MPH. The resolution passed unanimously, with Pauline Blake abstaining. Passedminutes ↗
Full text

175 3rd Street​ David Briggs presented a motion to approve the certification to transfer development rights at 175 3rd Street. He explained that this project involves 971 units permitted as-of-right. Additionally, Charney Companies and Tavros plans to acquire zoning floor area (ZFA) from the neighboring Powerhouse Arts, which would enable construction of 100 additional units. This transfer of floor area from a landmarked building is allowed under the City of Yes zoning changes and the request before the Community Board concerns modifications to building bulk. Under City of Yes changes, this application will go directly to the City Planning Commission (CPC), bypassing the local council member and Borough President, with a CPC hearing scheduled for March 17.

ces, and Education committee meeting relevant to site selection and acquisition of land for the new Harbor Middle School and encouraged all to attend.   EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE………………............................................... oard Chair Sayar Lonial reported that the Finance, Personnel, and Law committee drafted, over the course of the summer, a new job description for the District Manager position, taking input from other Community Boards around the city, as well as other sources. The job description was reviewed, edited, and approved by the Executive Committee at its November meeting.

To approve the job description for the District Manager position. Discussion ensued, with various Board Members asking about the process of by which the Finance, Personnel, and Law committee drafted the description. Some questions about language were asked, and some Board Members suggested various alternatives to certain terms, particularly in the first three paragraphs of the description. Two friendly amendments were accepted: changing the first sentence from “This is a management class position” to “This is an at-will management class position” and the second sentence in the first numbered job responsibility, Supervision of Staff/District Office, from “The District Office processes inquiries…” to “The District Office processes and responds to inquiries…”.

Motion to approve the Department of Transportation’s proposal to upgrade the existing Bond Street bike lane between Douglass and 3rd Streets in the district. Board Member Paul Basile asked how many businesses curb cuts were impacted by the proposal. Committee Co-Chair McClure said we can ask DOT. Board Member Joe Ann Brown asked if there was any way to effectively separate bicycles and trucks. Board Member Paul Basile said this kind of treatment increases liability for businesses that use the space in front of their building for loading and unloading. Board Member Suzanne Turet stated that bicyclists need to make things safer for pedestrians, not more hazardous.

Motion to approve the Department of Transportation's plans to roll-out CitiBike, the City's bike share program, to the district. Board Members Paul Basile and Debra Buscarello both made the point that bicycles and trucks to not mix well so the City should avoid putting bicycle facilities along truck routes and by manufacturing businesses. Board Member Suzanne Turet asked how many parking spaces will be lost to the CitiBike program in our district calling the program “an assault on parking.” Committee Chair McClure roughly calculated approximately 100 spaces overall. Recommendation to disapprove a Certificate of Appropriateness application submitted to the Landmarks Preservation Commission for the rooftop installation of an elevated canopy solar energy system at 202 Warren Street (between Clinton/Henry Streets), Cobble Hill Historic District. Conversation ensued, most heavily relevant to Landmarks Preservation when considering energy alternatives. A significant number of board members expressed their concern with setting a precedent that de-incentivizes homeowners in Historic Districts from upgrading their energy supply to more modern and environmentally friendly standards. New York City Economic Development representatives: Lydia Downing, Justine Johnson, and Peter Flint made the presentation.

A motion was made by Jerry Armer and seconded by Madelaine Murphy. 1. eview of a Certificate of Appropriateness application submitted to the Landmarks Preservation Commission for the construction of a rooftop shade pergola at 620 10th Street (between 7th/8th Avenues), Park Slope Historic District. Applicant presented for a pergola attached to railing and beam with cedar strips on top, natural wood. It would go to the edge of the building. Hildegaard Link pointed out that with the pergola coming out to the building edge the required setback would effectively be eliminated and has a negative impact on light and air and increases the perceived bulk of the building.

A motion was made by Bill Blum and seconded by Hildegaard Link to disapprove the application as presented because with the pergola coming out to the building edge the required setback would effectively be eliminated and this has a negative impact on light and air and increases the perceived bulk of the building. However, disapproval is subject to the applicant’s withdrawal of its application from the LPC in which case the item will be deemed tabled.

Proposed by Matthew Silverman ...that DOT prioritize streets with bike lanes over other streets with comparable conditions.

Passed12–3–1 yeas–nays–abst.minutes ↗
Full text

sion with a representative for the Department of Transportation on the department’s roadway resurfacing services (i.e., how streets get resurfaced). Presentation by Chris Hrones, DOT on the milling/paving program. All roadways are rated on scale of 1 – 10 every 2 years. 10 is the best. 7 may trigger a repaving. 5 – 6 is a definite repaving. Community board input can help address priorities. DOT now going to each community board every year to discuss repaving needs. Used to be every 18 months. Street volumes also determine priority. Larger arterials may be prioritized over smaller side streets.

Proposed by Matthew Silverman ...that DOT prioritize streets with bike lanes over other streets with comparable conditions. Seconded by Eric McClure. Discussion. Motion withdrawn. Suggestion to modify language to include all “vulnerable street users.” MOTION: Proposed by Jerry Armer “In evaluating streets to prioritize for milling and repaving, DOT consider safety of vulnerable street users.” Question called.

Source: June 19, 2014 Minutes

ay.” Sara Weinbrom presented to the committee the proposal to co-name Fifth Street between Sixth and Seventh Avenues as “Barry Weinbrom Way” in honor of her father. The late Mr. Weinbrom was an active member of the Park Slope community with a passion for the environment. He was an educator teaching general sciences, environmental science, and biology in the New York City Department of Education for over thirty years. Matthew Silverman stated that Mr. Weinbrom’s interest in local environmental concerns was still relevant today. Judith Thompson commended Mr. Weinbrom for being ahead of his time.

A motion was made by Judith Thompson to endorse the proposal to co-name Fifth Street between Sixth and Seventh Avenues as “Barry Weinbrom Way,” seconded by Rosemary Graham.

Review of a new on-premises liquor license application submitted to the State Liquor Authority on behalf of The Fat Mermaid LLC at 307 Smith Street (between President/Union Streets) in our district. ENDANCE: PRESENT: J. ARMER W. BLUM P. FLEMING R. LEVINE T. MISKEL M. MURPHY R. OBERLENDER D. SCOTTO M. SHAMES R. SLOANE E. SPICER EXCUSED: G. KELLY D. KUMMER ABSENT: B. ATKINS P. BLAKE K. FREEMAN A. MESSINA *** MINUTES *** On-site visit and update on the Green-Wood Cemetery’s efforts to preserve the Battle Hill view corridor which visually connects the Minerva statue in Green-Wood Cemetery to the Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor (crossing through the southern portion of the Red Hook coastline as intervening space). There is a quorum present.

A motion was made by Jerry Armer to support sponsoring the application with Community Board 7 for a 197a plan to preserve the Battle Hill view corridor from the Minerva statue to the Statue of Liberty. It does not mean that we support final approval. The plan will come back to us for a formal public hearing and review under ULURP. The motion was seconded by Bill Blum.

March 22, 2010Business Affairs & Licensing (formerly Permits & Licenses)Liquor license

Discussion of Assembly Bill A 7364-c to amend the SLA regulations for calculating the 200 foot rule and 500 foot rule measurements for proposed on premise liquor establishments.

Passedminutes ↗
Full text

Discussion of Assembly Bill A 7364-c to amend the SLA regulations for calculating the 200 foot rule and 500 foot rule measurements for proposed on premise liquor establishments. The bill proposes a much stricter measurement of property line to property line (the shortest possible distance), rather than the current rule/measurement of door to door. The bill in the Assembly is now before the Economic Development Committee, while the Senate voted unanimously in favor of the bill. Also, whether an establishment can benefit from the public interest exception is now at least in part to be determined by the community board, which will be a factor. Motion to support the bill as currently written.

Source: March 22, 2010 Minutes

Motion: Recommend to LPC the conditional approval of the Berkeley Carroll School new building as presented.

Passedminutes ↗
Full text

Motion: Recommend to LPC the conditional approval of the Berkeley Carroll School new building as presented. Condition 1) That the school meets with the new board at 209 St Johns Place to discuss the fencing material, and 2) that the terms of use of the roof top play area between the school and the community be completed before the construction begins. Vote: Yes: 11, No: 4, Abs: 1. Motion PASSES Motion by Roy Sloane, seconded by Peter Fleming: That the Community Board establish a Working Group/Task Force made up of representative of the CB, surrounding buildings and the Berkeley Carroll School that would meet monthly to discuss and work out any problem that will occur during and before construction and to provide the community with a way to communicate with the school during the construction period. Vote: All in favor

Presentation made by applicant from the Clarett Group detailing why they were before the committee and asking that they be allowed to build the project as originally designed.

Passedminutes ↗
Full text

Presentation made by applicant from the Clarett Group detailing why they were before the committee and asking that they be allowed to build the project as originally designed. Because of the rezoning of recent Carroll Garden, the DOB issued a Stop Work Order and the applicant must go to the BSA to have the original plans vested. They explained that 100% of the foundation is completed and that they have not continued to build is because of the current economic climate and that fully intent to complete the project once construction funds/loans are available. A motion was made by J. Armer and seconded by T. Miskel: To recommend to BSA that the project as originally planned be vested and allowed to proceed.
